newsitem.title: FINLAND: AMER SAYS K-SHR REDEMPTION PRICING CORRECT.
newsitem.headline: AMER SAYS K-SHR REDEMPTION PRICING CORRECT.

text.p: Amer-yhtyma Oy said on Thursday that the pricing of the redemption of K-shares by its board had been based on Amer's articles of association, which in turn must be in line with current legislation.

Pekka Kainulainen, chairman of Amer's board of directors, told Reuters by telephone that the company by-laws stated that it may redeem the vote-heavy K shares offered for sale at the price agreed between the seller and a potential buyer, in this case British investor Jonathan Bryan Guinness, third Lord Moyne.
"The price announced to us was the price agreed between the buyer and the seller," he said.

Kainulainen was asked to comment on media reports that the pricing of the redemption of the 275,000 K shares offered in June to British investor Jonathan Bryan Guinness, third Lord Moyne, may have been against the law.

The redemption had been "studied so thoroughly" that all legal aspects must have been taken into consideration, he said, adding it was obvious that regulatory authorities would not approve company by-laws which contradicted legislation.
Lord Moyne had been offered 275,000 K shares by the Student Union of the Helsinki School of Economics and Business Administration. They had agreed a share price of 273.64 markka.
